newsitem.title: CHINA: China state debt depository aims to control risk.
newsitem.headline: China state debt depository aims to control risk.

text.p: China's new national state debt depository in which all investors and institutions are required to deposit treasury debt certificates will help improve risk control, the China Securities newspaper said on Tuesday.
"A unified national state debt depository will help estalish an effective supervision system," the newspaper said.
"Separation of securities trading and settlement is the standard means of controlling risk on the international financial markets," it said.

Beijing last Friday announced plans to set up the new depository, the China Government Securities Depository Trust and Clearing Co, which will be responsible for holding, clearing and settling all state debt transactions.

State debt settlement is currently handled by the stock exchanges and trading centres, which increases risk given the tough competition among the exchanges and centres for market share and turnover, the newspaper said.
The establishment of the national depository will gradually help to end the practice of short-selling using fake certificates, it added.

China's securities rules ban state debt margin trading, but in fact many local securities trading centres have allowed the practice with some only maintaining a three percent margin requirement, analysts said.
The illegal margin trading has caused billions of yuan in losses for some state-owned institutions, they said.
Industry sources said the central depository was an important element in Beijing's plans to set up a national state debt market.

The central government wants the STAQ computerised trading system, which now mainly trades institutional (non-public) shares, to take over state debt trading from local markets including the Shanghai stock exchange, sources said.
Last Friday, the Finance Ministry issued a set of rules governing the new depository, requiring all regional markets to transfer state debt certificates deposited locally to the central depository.
The rules come into effect immediately, but industry sources said it would need time for all local markets to transfer state debt certificates in their hands to the central depository.
